FORBIDDEN_INPUTS: downstream ADD / yaw / translation / IoU result
rule: 1. construct hypothesis A: camera-facing WIDTH is the physical long axis, edges (0,1)(2,3)(4,5)(6,7)
2. construct hypothesis B: camera-facing DEPTH is the physical long axis, edges (0,4)(1,5)(2,6)(3,7)
3. solve each independently from the GT keypoints with SQPnP then RefineLM
4. compute the same reprojection residual for each: mean Euclidean distance between reprojected model corners and annotated corners over supervised corners
5. select the hypothesis with the lower residual
6. retain the 180-degree sign as an equivalence class; it is never resolved
selection_criterion: lower reprojection residual on GT keypoints

symmetry.note: 90 degrees is never absorbed; a rotation that changes which face the forks enter is a different pose

quality_condition.source: scripts/annotate/_audit_annotate.py:200 — the repository's pre-existing annotation-quality bar

exclusion_policy.unresolved_only_when: solver failure — fewer than six usable corners, or SQPnP returns no solution
exclusion_policy.rationale: choosing a margin cut-off after seeing the distribution is the post-hoc selection this lock exists to prevent. Both hypothesis residuals and the margin are preserved per frame instead.

human_review.interpretation: the reviewer judged apparent image length, which under strong perspective foreshortening is not the same quantity as physical long-axis length. This is not described as human error.

withdrawn_diagnosis.claim: at low elevation the axis identification is impossible in principle
withdrawn_diagnosis.reason: not supported by measurement — with annotated keypoints and known geometry the two hypotheses separate by residual in almost every frame, including at 0-2 degrees elevation
